properties.headline: Wildfire with IMMEDIATE EVACUATION for Velma.
properties.description: At 2:10 PM  a large and destructive wildfire was burning out of control W of Velma spreading rapidly NE. Wildfires can damage or destroy structures and can harm or kill people and animals. For your safety EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY for The Stephens County Fairgrounds.
properties.instruction:
Those between Sanner Road and Hargrove Street should LEAVE this area NOW to avoid injury or death. Do not delay to pack belongings. Reunification Center is setting up at Stephens County Fairgrounds.
Roads in the area may be impacted by fire and smoke. Never drive into heavy smoke. SLOW DOWN & MOVE OVER for emergency vehicles.

CMAMtext: Stephens CO EM: EVACUATION ORDER for Location for a wildfire. LEAVE NOW to the Direction.
CMAMlongtext: Jurisdiction EM: A dangerous wildfire is located Location spreading rapidly Direction. This area is in IMMEDIATE DANGER from wildfires which can cause injury/death, burn down homes/other structures. LEAVE NOW toward the Evacuation Center. Do not delay to pack belongings. Never drive into heavy smoke.

properties.description:
SMWMHX

The National Weather Service in Newport has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Pamlico Sound...
S of Cape Hatteras NC to Ocracoke Inlet NC out to 20 NM...
S of Ocracoke Inlet NC to Cape Lookout NC out to 20 NM...

* Until 600 PM EDT.

* At 459 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near The Vicinity Of Davis, or near Drum
Inlet, moving east at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to nearly 50 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
The Vicinity Of Atlantic, Ar255, The Vicinity Of Davis, Drum Inlet,
and Ar275.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 24 at 2:43PM MDT until August 24 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Garfield County in southern Utah...
North Central Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 645 PM MDT.

* At 243 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across portions of Bryce Canyon National Park, with
flows likely extending down Sheep Creek and the Paria River. Up to
1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams, slot
canyons, and normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Bryce Canyon National Park, including areas near Sheep Creek, the
Paria River, Bull Valley Gorge, Willis Creek, and Herm Pollock Slot
Canyon.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 6:45 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 6:45 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 24 at 1:34PM MDT until August 24 at 4:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Babylon burn scar in...
Central San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* Until 430 PM MDT.

* At 134 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Babylon Burn Scar over Dark Canyon. Between 0.5
and 0.8 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1
to 3 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation
and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Babylon Burn Scar over
Dark Canyon.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Babylon Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Dark Canyon
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Babylon Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
through slot canyons and steep terrain below Dark Canyon..climb to
safety.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging currents in a matter
of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 4:30 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:30 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.
